name: Hawking Temperature
description: Compute the Hawking radiation temperature T = ℏc³ / (8πGMk_B) for a black hole of mass M. This is the flagship bridge tile: semantic_confidence = 1.0 because the connection is an exact physical identity, not analogy — the same formula connects a gravitational event horizon to a thermal photon bath. All four constants (ℏ, c, G, k_B) are preloaded from the CODATA 2018 table. The result is a temperature in Kelvin; for a solar-mass black hole (~2×10³⁰ kg) this gives ~6×10⁻⁸ K. SI_CHECK enforces dimensional correctness: [ℏ][c³]/([G][M][k_B]) = J·s·(m/s)³/(m³·kg⁻¹·s⁻²·kg·J·K⁻¹) = K ✓.
author: system

pipeline.note: T = ℏc³/(8πGMk_B): composed MIF arithmetic on preloaded constants + M input
Dimensional check: result unit must be K

validation: M = M_sun (1.989×10³⁰ kg) → T ≈ 6.17×10⁻⁸ K. M = 1 kg → T ≈ 1.23×10²³ K. T ∝ 1/M: doubling mass halves temperature.
bridge_note: This model is the reference point for the FlowTrix-PhysTrix bridge: the same T appears as the thermal bath temperature in a Stefan-Boltzmann radiation model, connecting the gravitational domain (mass, event horizon) to the thermal diffusion domain via semantic_confidence = 1.0.
